title: Authentication
snippet:
Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.
The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.
## Getting Your API Token
API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.
Click **New Token**.
Enter a descriptive **token name** and choose an **expiration date**.
Click **Create**, then copy and securely store the generated token.
Keep Your Token Secure
## Authenticating Requests
Include your API token in the `x-api-token` HTTP header on every request:
```
x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```
### Marketplace Endpoints
For [Marketplace endpoints](https://app.mrscraper.com/marketplace), authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 `Authorization` header with a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```
## Verify Token
To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the [`/subscription-accounts`](***REDACTED*** endpoint:
```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \
-H "accept: application/json" \
-H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```
## Analytics Authentication
[Analytics endpoints](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/analytic/status) authenticate using the same `x-api-token` header as all other API endpoints.
When querying analytics, you can also pass the `apiTokenName` query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it:
```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME" \
-H "accept: application/json" \

title: GitHub - mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp: Official MrScraper MCP server: Scraper API for HTML, Markdown, and screenshots, web search, and account usage for AI agents.
LangChain SDK
snippet:
## Authentication
Set your API token from the [MrScraper dashboard](/docs/getting-started/api-token) as an environment variable:
```
import os
os.environ["MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN"] = "MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN"
```
Authentication Options
For more information on generating API tokens, see the [Generate Token](/docs/getting-started/api-token) guide.
## Quick Start
### Using MrScraperToolkit
Load all available tools with the toolkit:
```
from langchain_mrscraper import MrScraperToolkit
# Using environment variable
tools = MrScraperToolkit().get_tools()
# Or with explicit token
tools = MrScraperToolkit(token="MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN").get_tools()
```
### Using Convenience Loader
Alternatively, use the convenience function:
```
from langchain_mrscraper import load_mrscraper_tools
tools = load_mrscraper_tools()
```
### Using with AI Agents
```
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_mrscraper import MrScraperToolkit
# Load MrScraper tools
tools = MrScraperToolkit(token="MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN").get_tools()
# Create agent with OpenAI
agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), tools)
# Use the agent
response = agent.invoke({
"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Fetch the HTML from https://example.com"}]
})
```

### Token Management
Store your API token securely:
```
import os
from pathlib import Path
# Load from .env file
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()
token = os.getenv("MRSCRAPER_API_KEY")
```

title: CLI
snippet:
Install, authenticate, and use the MrScraper CLI to retrieve pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots, search Google, and check account usage.
The MrScraper CLI provides terminal access to page retrieval, Google search, and account usage. This guide covers installation, verification, authentication, output formats, environment variables, programmatic usage, and complete command details.
## Requirements
- Node.js 20 or newer
- A MrScraper account for browser login, or an API key for non-interactive use

### Copyable AI setup prompt
```
Read and follow https://github.com/mrscraper-com/cli/blob/main/skills/mrscraper/SKILL.md
```
For an agent-controlled, non-interactive setup, skip authentication during bootstrap and start login separately:
```
npx -y @mrscraper/cli@latest init --agent codex --yes --skip-auth
mrscraper auth status --json
mrscraper login
```

## Authentication
### Browser login
```
mrscraper login
```
The CLI opens the MrScraper login page, waits for the local browser callback, exchanges the returned code, and saves the provisioned API key in `~/.mrscraper/auth.json`. Set `MRSCRAPER_HOME` to change the containing directory.
### API-key login
```
mrscraper login --api-key "$MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
```
Prefer environment variables to literal keys in shell history:
```
export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY="your-key"
```
Authentication precedence for API commands is:
1. Command `--token`
2. `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`
3. `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN`
4. `~/.mrscraper/auth.json`
### `login` parameters
| Parameter | Default | Scope | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--api-key <key>` | — | Local | Saves this API key and does not open browser login. |
| `--token <key>` | — | Local | Deprecated alias for login's `--api-key`. |
| `--no-browser` | off | Local | Prompts a human for an API key; requires an interactive terminal. |
| `--no-open` | off | Local | Prints the browser URL without launching it. The callback server still waits. |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | `180` | Local | Maximum time to wait for the browser callback. |
### Auth status and logout
`mrscraper auth status` reports the credential currently available to the CLI. It reads the local configuration without sending a test request. JSON output uses the `credential_configured` field:
```
{
"credential_configured": true,
"auth_type": "api_key",
"path": "/home/user/.mrscraper/auth.json"
}
```

| `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` | — | Preferred API-key environment override. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` | — | Alternative API-key environment override

title: Authenticate Web Data Tools for AI Agents Without Exposing Secrets
snippet:
Most teams use one of two patterns:
1. **Your backend owns the key.** Your server holds a MrScraper API token. The agent calls your tools, and your server calls MrScraper.
2. **Each user connects their own account.** A person signs in to MrScraper through their MCP client, such as Claude Code or Codex. The client handles the sign-in, and the agent uses that person's access. The next section covers when to use each one.
## **When should you use API keys or OAuth?**
| Use an API key when | Use OAuth when |
|---|---|
| Your app calls MrScraper on its own behalf | A person connects their own MrScraper account |
| The call runs on your server, a job runner or CI | The call runs from that person's MCP client |
| One account pays for and owns the usage | Each person's usage should stay on their account |
| You control where the key is stored | You do not want anyone to copy or paste a key |
### **API keys for your backend**
MrScraper API tokens are created in the dashboard under **API Tokens**. Each token has a name and an expiration date. You can create more than one, so you can give each environment or app its own token. See the [API token docs](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/api-token) for the steps.
The REST API reads the token from the `x-api-token` header. The Scraper API examples also pass it as a `token` query parameter. Your server sends both. The agent never sees either.
### **OAuth for people using MCP clients**
The hosted [MrScraper MCP server](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` supports OAuth 2.1. The client opens a browser, the person signs in, and no key is copied anywhere.
To add it in Claude Code:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
To add it in Codex:
bash
```bash
codex mcp add mrscraper --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
OAuth access uses scopes:
- **`scrape:read`** covers the `scraperAPI` and `webSearch` tools.
- **`account:read`** covers the `status` tool. If a client calls a tool without the right scope, the server refuses it with a 403 `insufficient_scope` error. Grant only the scopes a person needs.

If your agent runs in a web app, the browser should talk to your server, never to MrScraper. Your server checks who the user is, then runs the tool.
text
```text
Browser  ->  Your server (checks user, runs tool)  ->  MrScraper API
holds MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN
```
